I am interested in installing linux on my gaming pc, and I'm thinking of going with ubuntu. Is there a better user-friendly distro for gaming?
Maybe SteamOS. Or Ubuntu with the real time kernel.

What benifit would the real time kernel give?

Does anyone actually notice lag from ther kernel processes? I know it was a problem in the past but is it still an issue?

Last time i used a realtime kernel was to drive a big robot at 80Hz and i could have done everything with vanilla posix threads and the standard kernel. The realtime threads/kernel was there just to ensure that if a thread missed an execution deadline the robot wouldn't try to go backwards or try to execute commands out of sequence

Drivers are part of the kernel. The proprietary drivers from Nvidia and AMD are binary blobs, while the open source drivers are a normal part of the kernel, available in source. Realtime kernal are tweaked to a short reaction time.

Realtime is for determinism (high priority 100hz loop is executed always at 100.00000hz +/-.00001hz) if you want balls to the wall speed you should be using the low latency kernel which drops the delays in the kernel to minimums (delays are left in for other processes drivers/timers/userprograms to interupt to get things done)

But dont take my word for it :

https://help.ubuntu.com/community/UbuntuStudio/RealTimeKernel

And www.mvista.com/download/vision08/Real-time-vs-real-fast-Vision2008.pdf

If nvidias blobs need determinism for best performance ok realtime kernel all the way

Otherwwise its like putting a dodge viper engine on an 18 wheeler sure the engine can go fast but cant pull shit

Sorry to bug you about this i just keep seeing people saying use the realtime kernel and i never see the rationale for it

The real time kernel is optimized on reaction speed to interrupts, the should be processed below a certain amount of ms. This has the tradeoff that other tasks of the kernel can perform worse because they are stopped to handle interrupts more often. If it's better for gaming when the usb input is processed 10 ms sooner but the memory management takes longer probably depends on the game and the hardware. Such things are hard to benchmark, there is no good, fact based recommendation for gaming. In other areas, like robotics or driving assistance system for example the real time kernel is more clearly the better choice.
